answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Signed npm package maintainer record with registry attestation flips the bet — packages the registry recorded under one maintainer for years — and the reef lands on the attacker instead. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the willow of that gap is the whole defence in one line. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The comet grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
